Stage rehearsal game. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor technician starts at (1,1). Station cuePad is at (2,1), station finishPad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object propCabinet at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by technician. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially propCabinet is locked, flags started and missed are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 400 ticks.
An effective activation of cuePad, while not started, not missed, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
The started timer runs for exactly 20 seconds.
An effective activation of finishPad unlocks propCabinet and stops the timer only if started is true, missed is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, missed is false and the object remains locked, set missed to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating finishPad before cuePad has no effect. Repeated activation of cuePad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.
input.intervention: Experiment with a 6-second timer instead of 20 seconds. Keep the original source and all other rules. Compare the same visitor actions in both branches.

Observatory training game. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor operator starts at (1,1). Station calibratePad is at (2,1), station capturePad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object imageArchive at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by operator. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially imageArchive is locked, flags started and expired are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 280 ticks.
An effective activation of calibratePad, while not started, not expired, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
An effective activation of capturePad unlocks imageArchive and stops the timer only if started is true, expired is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, expired is false and the object remains locked, set expired to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating capturePad before calibratePad has no effect. Repeated activation of calibratePad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.
input.intervention: Experiment with a 4-second timer instead of 14 seconds. Keep the original source and all other rules. Compare the same visitor actions in both branches.
input.clarification: The started timer runs for exactly 14 seconds; the declared capacity alone does not specify the start duration.

Workshop assembly game. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor builder starts at (1,1). Station beginPad is at (2,1), station inspectPad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object partsLocker at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by builder. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially partsLocker is locked, flags started and failed are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 360 ticks.
An effective activation of beginPad, while not started, not failed, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
An effective activation of inspectPad unlocks partsLocker and stops the timer only if started is true, failed is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, failed is false and the object remains locked, set failed to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating inspectPad before beginPad has no effect. Repeated activation of beginPad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.
input.intervention: Experiment with a 6-second timer instead of 18 seconds. Keep the original source and all other rules. Compare the same visitor actions in both branches.
input.clarification: The started timer runs for exactly 18 seconds; the declared capacity alone does not specify the start duration.

Animation studio game. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor artist starts at (1,1). Station startPad is at (2,1), station deliverPad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object assetVault at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by artist. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially assetVault is locked, flags started and late are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 240 ticks.
An effective activation of startPad, while not started, not late, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
An effective activation of deliverPad unlocks assetVault and stops the timer only if started is true, late is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, late is false and the object remains locked, set late to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating deliverPad before startPad has no effect. Repeated activation of startPad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.
input.intervention: Experiment with a 4-second timer instead of 12 seconds. Keep the original source and all other rules. Compare the same visitor actions in both branches.
input.clarification: The started timer runs for exactly 12 seconds; the declared capacity alone does not specify the start duration.

Aquarium maintenance game. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor attendant starts at (1,1). Station checkPad is at (2,1), station recordPad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object toolCabinet at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by attendant. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially toolCabinet is locked, flags started and expired are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 320 ticks.
An effective activation of checkPad, while not started, not expired, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
Procedure A says the started timer runs for exactly 16 seconds. Procedure B says it runs for exactly 13 seconds. Both statements are authoritative and this source does not choose between them.
An effective activation of recordPad unlocks toolCabinet and stops the timer only if started is true, expired is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, expired is false and the object remains locked, set expired to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating recordPad before checkPad has no effect. Repeated activation of checkPad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.
input.intervention: Experiment with a 5-second timer instead of 16 seconds. Keep the original source and all other rules. Compare the same visitor actions in both branches.
input.clarification: For this run use Procedure A: the started timer runs for exactly 16 seconds. This explicit clarification supersedes Procedure B.

The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor attendant starts at (1,1). Station checkPad is at (2,1), station recordPad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object toolCabinet at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by attendant. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially toolCabinet is locked, flags started and expired are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 320 ticks.
An effective activation of checkPad, while not started, not expired, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.

An effective activation of recordPad unlocks toolCabinet and stops the timer only if started is true, expired is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.

Activating recordPad before checkPad has no effect. Repeated activation of checkPad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.

input.source:
Warehouse dispatch game. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor clerk starts at (1,1). Station labelPad is at (2,1), station handoffPad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object loadingGate at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by clerk. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially loadingGate is locked, flags started and late are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 400 ticks.
An effective activation of labelPad, while not started, not late, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
Procedure A says the started timer runs for exactly 20 seconds. Procedure B says it runs for exactly 17 seconds. Both statements are authoritative and this source does not choose between them.
An effective activation of handoffPad unlocks loadingGate and stops the timer only if started is true, late is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, late is false and the object remains locked, set late to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating handoffPad before labelPad has no effect. Repeated activation of labelPad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.

The engine already creates canonical moveTo inputs to entities with sockets. Do not emit extra moveTo rules or invent a movement configuration. This built-in behavior needs no source rule binding. Do not put goals or descriptive prose in sim fields.
Example below illustrates syntax only and has different behavior from the source. Do not copy its identifiers, duration, outcome, or evidence; generate the source behavior. Emit sim itself under the reply sim field, not another WorldDoc wrapper.
{"layout":{"kind":"room","width":5,"height":3},"grid":{"cell":1},"sockets":{"spawn":[0,1],"button":[1,1],"exit":[4,1]},"collisionAabb":{},"entities":{"operator":{"role":"actor","socket":"spawn"},"button":{"role":"sensor","socket":"button"},"gate":{"role":"display","socket":"exit","locked":true}},"state":{"flags":{"started":false},"timers":{"window":{"durationTicks":40,"initial":0}},"zones":{"adjacent":[[0,1,1,1],[2,1,1,1],[1,0,1,1],[1,2,1,1]]}},"rules":{"press":{"event":{"kind":"onAction","actionId":"press","target":"button"},"condition":{"kind":"allOf","operands":[{"kind":"flagIs","ref":"started","value":false},{"kind":"inZone","entity":"operator","zone":"adjacent"},{"kind":"lockedIs","target":"gate","value":true}]},"actions":[{"kind":"setFlag","ref":"started","value":true},{"kind":"setLocked","target":"gate","value":false},{"kind":"startTimer","ref":"window","durationTicks":40}]},"expiry":{"event":{"kind":"onTimerEnd","timer":"window"},"condition":{"kind":"flagIs","ref":"started","value":true},"actions":[{"kind":"setLocked","target":"gate","value":true}]}},"witness":{"tier":"short","ops":[]}}
sim contains layout {kind,width,height}, grid {cell}, sockets, collisionAabb, entities, state, rules (ID-keyed map), witness.
Rules explicitly contain event, condition and actions; use existing surface operations only, never executable code.
Before writing rules, check trigger, initial state, proximity, duration/unit, expiration, reset/repetition, outcome and same-tick ordering.
If a critical condition is missing, put a concrete question in missingCritical and return sim:null. Never invent a critical assumption.
List conflicting source statements in conflicts; do not choose one. Put unsupported mechanics in unsupported; do not approximate them.
Any nonempty missingCritical/conflicts/unsupported list blocks execution. Claims may still describe the source.
Every rule requires an evidence binding. All claim reviews must be {status:"unchecked"}; interventionId:null.
Sourced claims use exact UTF-8 byte spans [startByte,endByte) with excerpt and sourceId from the envelope.
Derived claims name premises and derivation. Assumed claims explicitly describe only noncritical layout/presentation choices.
The runtime is 20 Hz. Convert seconds to exact integer ticks; unsupported fractional ticks require clarification.
Timeout wins over activation on the same tick. Input N is visible in snapshot N+1. Do not claim other timing semantics.
JSON validity and exact citations do not prove semantic truth; do not mark a proposal reviewed or certified.

{"sourceId":"source","text":"Warehouse dispatch game. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor clerk starts at (1,1). Station labelPad is at (2,1), station handoffPad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object loadingGate at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by clerk. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially loadingGate is locked, flags started and late are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 400 ticks.
An effective activation of labelPad, while not started, not late, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
Procedure A says the started timer runs for exactly 20 seconds. Procedure B says it runs for exactly 17 seconds. Both statements are authoritative and this source does not choose between them.
An effective activation of handoffPad unlocks loadingGate and stops the timer only if started is true, late is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, late is false and the object remains locked, set late to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating handoffPad before labelPad has no effect. Repeated activation of labelPad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.

Clarification: For this run use Procedure A: the started timer runs for exactly 20 seconds. This explicit clarification supersedes Procedure B."}
